outcomes.resolution_summary: DART successfully impacted Dimorphos, and NASA measured an orbital-period reduction of roughly 32 minutes, far exceeding the 73-second minimum success criterion.

authoritative_sources.title: Final Technical Report for the Double Asteroid Redirection Test Mission

cruxes.description: Whether DART's autonomous navigation could identify and strike Dimorphos accurately enough to execute the experiment.
Whether the impact and ejecta would transfer enough momentum to exceed the minimum measurable orbital-period change.
Whether the observing campaign could determine the post-impact binary period precisely enough to verify the threshold.

outcomes.resolution_summary: NOAA's post-season monitoring recorded 20 Atlantic named storms in 2023, above the 1991-2020 average of 14.

authoritative_sources.title: NOAA Global Ocean Monitoring: Recent Evolution, Current Status, and Predictions

cruxes.description: Whether developing El Nino wind shear would suppress Atlantic storm formation strongly enough to cap the seasonal count.
Whether exceptionally warm tropical Atlantic sea-surface temperatures would offset the expected El Nino suppression.
Whether environmental conditions would support numerous named storms even without an unusually high major-hurricane count.

outcomes.resolution_summary: NASA stood down from Psyche's 2022 launch opportunity after late flight-software delivery, immature testbeds, incomplete verification, and operations-readiness concerns.

authoritative_sources.title: Psyche Independent Review Board Report and NASA-JPL Response

cruxes.description: Whether guidance, navigation, control, and fault-protection software would reach a testable flight configuration with sufficient margin.
Whether the spacecraft simulators and verification program were mature enough to complete required validation before the launch window.
Whether the project and institution had enough experienced personnel to close technical and operations-readiness work safely.

outcomes.resolution_summary: Starliner's first crewed flight test did not launch by July 2023; after additional delays, it launched in June 2024.

authoritative_sources.title: NASA's Management of Risks to Sustaining ISS Operations through 2030

cruxes.description: Whether the remaining spacecraft technical issues could be resolved before fueling and final flight-readiness decisions.
Whether the July target retained enough schedule margin for NASA and Boeing certification work without accepting excess crew risk.
Whether ISS traffic and mission-integration constraints would still support the targeted crew-flight window after technical slips.
